hook.text: Windmills emerged in Persia around the 9th century—vertical-axis designs that ground grain using desert winds.

buildup.text: European windmills (12th century) used horizontal-axis designs—sails mounted on a rotating cap that faced the wind.

discovery.text: The Netherlands built thousands of windmills to pump water—draining lakes and marshes to create farmland.

twist.text: Dutch windmills powered entire industries—sawmills, oil presses, paper mills, and dye works clustered near them.

climax.text: By 1750, the Netherlands had about 10,000 windmills—the world's first wind-powered industrial economy.

punchline.text: Wind turned blades, blades turned industry—the original wind power.
